x402.bareProbe: A bare GET (no query) or zero-byte POST with no payment header on any paid URL returns HTTP 402 at once: the v1 JSON body (x402Version 1, network base, maxAmountRequired) plus the v2 PAYMENT-REQUIRED header (x402Version 2, network eip155:8453, amount, extensions.bazaar with a JSON Schema draft 2020-12 schema).

settlement.note: A settled call returns 200 with both PAYMENT-RESPONSE and X-PAYMENT-RESPONSE (base64 {success, transaction, network, payer}). That receipt is the facilitator's settlement assertion bound to the payer; the MCP client checks it against the signed authorization but does not look the transaction up on Base (onchainReceiptVerified: false).

settlementGuard.replay: every credited Base USDC transfer is owned by one PactaLedgerDO Durable Object (tx:<txHash>, SQLite-backed, single-threaded), so a settlement transaction is credited once; any other claim on it is refused (402 replay_settlement_tx / 409 tx_already_used)
settlementGuard.requires: receipt status 0x1 and canonical USDC (Base) Transfer(payer -> payTo) logs summing to at least the route price

x402.settlementGuardNote: The gateway verifies every paid settlement on Base before releasing the product: eth_getTransactionReceipt must show status 0x1 and canonical USDC Transfer(payer -> payTo 0x4348DF1BEFAffcbA248B5118B1b782B1B2bdEd14) logs summing to at least the route price, and each credited transaction is owned by one PactaLedgerDO Durable Object (tx:<txHash>), so it is never credited twice (402 replay_settlement_tx). Otherwise the product is withheld: 402 unconfirmed_or_reverted_settlement_tx / insufficient_onchain_usdc_transfer, or 502 settlement_rpc_unavailable when no Base RPC answers.
